Variants.Content: In 214 BC, King Philip V of Macedon capitalized on Roman weakness following Cannae to strike Roman protectorates in Illyria, sparking the First Macedonian War. Unable to spare legions from Italy, Rome formed a formidable diplomatic alliance with the Aetolian League, Sparta, and Pergamon, embroiling Philip in regional warfare across Greece and preventing his Macedonian phalanxes from reinforcing Hannibal.
